verdicts.claim: An automatic checkpoint runs after a COMMIT that leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more. It runs on the thread that made the COMMIT, always in PASSIVE
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more'; 'run automatically by the same thread that does the COMMIT'; c3ref: 'Checkpoints initiated by this mechanism are PASSIVE.'

verdicts.claim: The default auto-checkpoint threshold is 1000 pages, about 4 MB. ... Zero or a negative value turns automatic checkpoints off.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'about 1000 pages (and is thus about 4MB in size)'; c3ref: 'Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint returns one row with three integers ... Columns 2 and 3 are -1 when the database is not in WAL mode.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'returns a single row with three integer columns ... The second and third column are -1 if there is no write-ahead log'

verdicts.claim: PRAGMA journal_size_limit ... The default is -1, which means no limit. Zero truncates them to their minimum size.
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'The default journal size limit is -1 (no limit)'; 'To always truncate ... to their minimum size, set the journal_size_limit to zero.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE also shrinks the WAL file to zero bytes on success.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: Litestream runs three checkpoint tiers. checkpoint-interval ... 1 minute ... 1000 pages (about 4 MB) ... truncate-page-n, at 121,359 pages (about 500 MB)
verdicts.evidence: guide: 'checkpoint-interval: 1m # Default: 1 minute'; 'min-checkpoint-page-count: 1000 # Default: ~4MB'; 'WAL exceeds 121,359 pages (~500MB)'; 'Attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint first, then falls back to a TRUNCATE'

verdicts.claim: SQLite says the WAL-reset bug is likely present in every release from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09).
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'The bug is likely present in all version of SQLite from 3.7.0 (2010-07-21) through 3.51.2 (2026-01-09).'

verdicts.claim: The WAL-reset bug is fixed in SQLite 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. SQLite backported the fix to 3.44.6 and 3.50.7. The 3.51.3 and 3.53.0 logs list
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'fixed in version 3.51.3 (2026-03-13) and later. Backports ... 3.44.6 and 3.50.7'; both release logs: 'Fix the WAL-reset database corruption bug.'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale says the WAL-reset fix first shipped in SQLite 3.52.0. SQLite's release log lists 3.52.0 (2026-03-06) as Withdrawn, features moved to 3.53.0
verdicts.evidence: 3.52.0 log: 'On 2026-03-06 Withdrawn ... features ... moved forward into version 3.53.0'; Tailscale: 'released the fix as SQLite 3.52.0' and 'withdrew the 3.52.0 release and instead published 3.51.3'

verdicts.claim: Tailscale counted 19 corruption incidents over six months before the underlying bug was resolved.
verdicts.evidence: Tailscale: 'we faced 19 separate instances of database corruption over six months before we finally resolved the underlying bug.'
